findings.reason: a coordinator driving the plan from its open followup dispatches landed sections and never dispatches §26, so the section the plan has just added goes unbuilt; this is the same recurrence the earlier reviews answered by rewriting the open followup.
findings.text: f-wftl-005, the plan's only open followup, is titled "Build §3, §6, §9, §12, §18, §20 to §25" and its body gives §6, §12, §18, §20 and §21 as "complete and in review, repair or landing", while the declarations at plan.html:23 now mark s6, s12, s18, s20, s21, s23 and s25 `done` and add s26 as `implementable`; the unbuilt set is §3, §9, §22, §24 and §26, and §26 is named by no followup

findings.reason: one of the two accepted categories is never exercised, so a run whose trailing commit touched only a figure is still refused and the section's own accepted set is unimplemented.
findings.text: the deliverable accepts an after arm when the intervening commits change only "the run's own evidence fragment or figure paths", but all four cases plant an evidence fragment or a source file or a test file, and none plants a commit that changes only a figure path, so an implementation that admits the fragment and refuses a figure-only commit passes the whole gate while the deliverable says that commit is accepted

findings.reason: the plural clause is the one that matters when a worker's assessment commit follows its evidence commit, and a two-commit interval holding one source-touching commit must be shown refused.
findings.text: every case plants exactly one commit between the arm's recorded revision and the head, so the deliverable's rule over "every commit between that revision and the head" is never exercised with more than one, and an implementation that inspects only the head's immediate parent — or only the last commit — passes all four cases and the negative control

findings.reason: the stated cause fixes the section's benefit as removing a resume when the mechanism it actually replaces is an expensive landing-side re-measurement, and a worker implementing the accept-rule without knowing which path left those two runs resuming cannot show the cost it exists to remove is gone.
findings.text: §26's Why states the arm "is refused as `after_suite.revision_matches_head`, and only a resumed worker turn can clear it, by re-running the same tests over the same code", but §17 — landed at `05c8f2d152` and declared done — makes the landing run the armed command itself at the revision it needs and land or refuse on that measurement, and `reckon/crew/promotion_records.py:1157` calls `_measure_missing_arms` whenever that field is in the missing set, so the landed alternative to the refusal is a landing-side re-measurement and not a resume; the section does not say why that path declined for the §18 and §25 runs it cites

response_events.note: Traced: §17's landing-side measurement did run for §18 and §23. Their after arms read 55 and 80 passed, EXIT=0. Their base arms were red, as expected when the new tests are absent, and srun appended 'srun: error: ... Exited with exit code 1' after the EXIT=1 receipt. The receipt is read only as the log's final line, so both measured pairs were unreadable and the landing fell back to refusing. §26 is rewritten around that cause.
§26 no longer carries an evidence-commit acceptance rule, so no figure-only case is owed. Its done-when now tests the measured-arm receipt that the cause above names.
